protocol.evaluation: Offline visual-goal planning; predictions were not executed on the robot.
protocol.reference: Recorded onboard odometry in meters; approximate visual camera alignment.
protocol.selection: Continuous 20–30 s clips preselected for scene coverage and unobstructed third-person view before evaluation.
protocol.planning: Each local plan starts from recorded context; both models share goals, horizon and CEM budget within each clip.
protocol.metrics: Paper ATE/RPE definitions, averaged across complete local plans. Different planning horizons are reported separately.
protocol.sampling: Original DDPM checkpoints; no DMD2. Budget and exact settings are retained per clip.

visualization.third_person: Dominant full-aspect video; high-quality SDR conversion where required.
visualization.gt_ego: High-resolution recorded frames with the same center crop as model input, shown at matched 4 Hz timestamps.
visualization.model: Exact saved generated frames, repeated at output FPS; no image enhancement or replacement.
visualization.sampling: Nearest 4 Hz sample shared by GT/model/trajectory; third-person follows aligned continuous time.
visualization.trajectory: Forward up, physical left to the left. Equal metric scale shared by all three paths, fit per local plan; no smoothing.

summary.aggregation: Unweighted mean over independent local-plan windows; no per-clip selection by model output.

quality.selection: The same one-second horizon is used for both models across all eight preselected clips after paired 1 s / 2 s visual review.
quality.limitations: One-second plans limit autoregressive drift; structural hallucinations remain in the unaltered model rollouts. Metrics compare offline plans with recorded Go2 odometry, not executed navigation.
quality.metric_comparison: Shorter-horizon errors are inherently easier; do not compare these one-second errors directly with two-second results as evidence of improved navigation.
quality.comparison_limitations: The1s and2s diagnostics share actual start times and recorded context, but have different goal frames, CEM horizons and ID-based random seeds. They are practical qualitative protocol checks, not a noise-matched horizon ablation. ATE/RPE across horizons must not be interpreted as a controlled accuracy improvement.
